inputs.share_count_basis: PRO FORMA ESTIMATE for the November 2026 ASR. Start: 51.023M shares on the Q3 2026 10-Q cover (2026-11-03) plus ~0.1M treasury-method dilution (Q3 2026 weighted diluted 51.469M vs basic 51.428M; the spread has run 0.04-0.26M) = ~51.1M. Less ~3.1M for the $500M ASR announced 2026-11-05 and executed the week of 2026-11-09, at an assumed all-in average of ~$160/share (an initial delivery of roughly 80% plus a final settlement on the VWAP over the term). The full $500M is deducted from net cash, so the full share delivery is credited here; one without the other would misstate value. The ASR is NOT in the Q3 10-Q (filed before execution) -- it rests on the Q3 earnings release as recorded in the Analysis JSON, and is corroborated by management's 49.9M Q4 weighted diluted share guide. Replace with the 10-K cover count when filed. Held FLAT thereafter because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $1.8B authorisation through 2029 is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat. The prior build's 52.2M carried ~0.5M too much dilution over the 2026-07-31 cover count (51.587M); that is corrected here and shown in the reconciliation.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q3 2026 10-Q (2026-09-30): cash and equivalents $965.2M + short-term investments $4.6M = $969.8M; revolver borrowings $25.0M; net cash $944.8M. Pro forma for the $500M ASR prepayment: net cash $444.8M. The cash/debt split of the ASR funding is not yet disclosed ('cash on hand and credit-facility borrowings'); $250M of revolver draw is ASSUMED for the total_debt and cash fields ($675M was undrawn at 9/30). Only the split is assumed -- net debt is the same whatever the mix. Q4 2026 free cash flow (seasonally the strongest quarter) is not credited.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement stock-based compensation add-back $176.8M plus $26.8M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities); EPAM publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure in its non-GAAP reconciliation, so the two lines are summed. 9M-2026: $138.8M + $23.2M = $162.0M (3.8% of revenue; withholding is front-loaded in H1, so the full year lands near 3.7%).
inputs.interest_income_source: Estimated. EPAM tags only a net 'Interest and other income, net' line ($46.9M FY2024, $11.5M FY2025, -$1.1M 9M-2026) which nets FX, contingent-consideration marks, impairments and interest expense against interest income. The interest component is estimated at ~3.2% on ~$1.2B average FY2025 cash. It is stripped from the FY2025 base; the forward build starts from EBITDA and so carries no interest income. After the ASR net cash (~$445M) is roughly 1x the owner-FCF base rather than 2x, and forward interest income will be materially lower and partly offset by revolver interest.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $662.2M; 9M-2026 $488.9M (3.891M shares, incl. the $300M March 2026 Morgan Stanley ASR). The $500M November 2026 ASR is on top of that, taking 2026 to ~$1.0B -- roughly twice a normal year's reported FCF, which is why it needed the revolver. Actual cash, not the $1.8B authorisation (through 2029-12-31).
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-11-03 cover count, pro forma for the 2026-11-09 ASR (estimate)
inputs.wacc_rationale: UNCHANGED at 10.5%. USD flows discounted at a USD rate: 10-year Treasury ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.3 gives a cost of equity ~10.7%. The ASR draw puts perhaps $250M of revolver debt against a ~$7.4B market cap (~3% debt/capital, still net cash of ~$445M), which moves a blended WACC by less than 0.1pp and adds no refinancing risk at this size, so the rate is not changed for the leverage shift. It would be revisited if EPAM moved to net debt above ~1x EBITDA to fund the $1.8B authorisation. No separate AI-risk premium is stacked on top: that risk is charged once, through the bear driver path and its 30% weight. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside EBITDA as an operating expense (operating lease liabilities $121M at 2026-09-30), so the lease charge is already in the flows; lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial at EPAM (single-digit $M); no NCI deduction and no attributable-flow adjustment.
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-09-28 build for Q3 2026 results (2026-11-05), the raised FY2026 guidance, and the November 2026 $500M ASR; see `reconciliation`. Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035), scenario-weighted -- unchanged. Routed via dcf-methods: EPAM is an operating IT-services/digital-engineering company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; none of the non-FCF rows apply and the adaptations file is not needed (USD filer, USD quote, leases inside EBITDA, no NCI, SBC-paying market). FY0 remains FY2025 (last completed year); year 1 is FY2026 at the raised guidance (revenue +3.5-3.7%, GAAP operating margin 10.7-10.9%, non-GAAP 15.9-16.1%). WHAT CHANGED: (1) anchors -- price, 9/30 balance sheet, share count, Belarus cash $37M -> $25.1M, all pro forma for the ASR; (2) year-1 drivers to guidance and 9M actuals: pre-SBC EBITDA 15.5% -> 16.3% (GAAP operating margin 10.8% + D&A 2.3% + SBC add-back 3.2%; 9M actual 16.0%, Q4 guided ~17.5%), SBC incl. withholding 3.9% -> 3.7%, D&A 2.2% -> 2.3%, capex 1.0% -> 1.1% (9M $47.7M); (3) later-year margin path lifted ~0.5pp in base because FY2026 already reaches the level the prior path took until FY2031 to get to (roughly half of the 0.8pp year-1 surprise is passed through, half treated as cost timing that the AI-native mix still has to prove durable); (4) base FY2027 growth 4.0% -> 3.5% and bull 7.0% -> 6.0% because the Q4 guide ($1.405-1.420B, flat to +0.9% YoY, down sequentially) sets an exit rate from which 4% needs ~1.7% sequential growth every quarter of 2027; (5) working-capital capture -10% -> -15%: 9M-2026 operating cash flow fell to $250M from $372M on $191M more revenue, with contract assets rising on milestone-billed work and fixed-price revenue up 18% YoY against T&M -1% -- outcome-based contracts carry a longer cash cycle. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth from FY2028 in all scenarios and the whole bear growth path (three large FS/Energy deals were signed, but they ramp in 2027 and replace rather than add to the prior assumption that pushed-out deals convert in H1 2027; Software & Hi-Tech, Business Information & Media and Consumer were all down YoY in Q3) -- FY2027 guidance in February 2027 is the evidence that would move them; the cash-tax ramp 31% -> 25% (no new cash-tax disclosure in the 10-Q; FY2026 10-K taxes paid would move it); terminal growth and cap multiples; WACC; scenario weights; and the bear terminal margin of 12%. KNOWN TIMING GAP: the build's FY2026 owner FCF (~$450M) is well above what FY2026 will actually print (9M reported FCF $202M vs $345M a year earlier; full-year owner FCF likely $250-300M) because of the 2026 working-capital build. The build treats that as timing plus the -15% capture; if DSO/contract assets do not recover in Q4 and FY2027, the margin path is ~$150M/yr too generous in the early years. Buybacks fund the flat count (repurchaser); at ~$150-160 the ASR was struck above this model's weighted value, which the pro forma anchors already capture (see the reconciliation bridge). Belarus cash ($25.1M) is deducted in the equity bridge; Ukraine cash ($28.3M) is not restricted and stays in net cash.

equity_bridge.item: Belarus-held cash subject to dividend restrictions
equity_bridge.note: Q3 2026 10-Q: $25.1M of cash in Belarusian banks at 2026-09-30 (down from ~$37M at FY2025); the April 2024 Belarusian restrictions on dividends to US shareholders are scheduled to run to the end of 2026. Haircut to zero pending relief or lapse. $28.3M in Ukrainian banks is not restricted and stays in net cash.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, cross-checked against the raised FY2026 guidance (3.5-3.7% reported, 2.5-2.7% organic constant currency). Equity 5yr CAGR (13.2%) is inflated by the 2020-22 digital boom and the 3yr figure (7.0%) is depressed by buybacks (~$1.7B returned since 2023), so neither is a clean forward proxy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.2% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 2.9% and from revenue 3yr CAGR 4.2%: the 2020-2022 boom (revenue +41% in FY2021, +28% in FY2022) is still inside the 5-year window while the 2023-2025 period was flat-to-recovering. The 3-year revenue CAGR is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr); unchanged from the prior build because no fiscal year has completed since. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC incl. equity-award taxes - interest income: FY2020 $376M (475.6 - 95.4 - ~4), FY2022 $244M (382.5 - 126.5 - ~12), FY2025 $371M (612.7 - 203.6 - ~38). Interest income before FY2024 is estimated from average cash and prevailing short rates (not separately tagged); the CAGRs move <1pp on any plausible alternative. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (-0.3%) sits far below reported FCF (+5.2%): SBC incl. withholding grew from $95M (2.8% of revenue) in FY2020 to $204M (3.7%) in FY2025, so an increasing share of reported cash generation is being paid to employees in stock. 9M-2026 reported FCF was $202M against $345M in 9M-2025: the FY2026 owner-FCF print will fall well short of FY2025 on working capital even as margins rise.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the 3.6% raised-guidance midpoint (was 3.7% on the wider prior range). FY2027 cut 4.0% -> 3.5%: the Q4 guide exits the year flat-to-+0.9% YoY, so even with the three new FS/Energy deals ramping, 3.5% already needs ~1.4% sequential growth each quarter. FY2028-29 unchanged at 5% as the AI-native book (13% of revenue and rising) and Financial Services (+13.7% YoY) carry the mix while Software & Hi-Tech keeps shrinking; then the unchanged glide to 2.5% as AI productivity compresses billable hours roughly in line with volume growth.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 16.3% in FY2026 (GAAP operating margin guide 10.7-10.9% + D&A 2.3% + SBC add-back 3.2%) drifting to 17.0% by FY2031 (was 16.5%) on delivery-mix shift to India/LatAm and AI-assisted utilisation gains that EPAM partly keeps. SBC anchored at 3.7% incl. withholding (FY2025 3.7%, 9M-2026 3.8%) and eased to 3.0%. Cash tax ramp unchanged, 31% -> 25%.
base.terminal_rationale: UNCHANGED. 2.5% terminal growth and a 15x owner-FCF cap: a labour-based services business facing AI deflation does not earn a 20x mature-compounder multiple.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of FY2026 guidance (3.7%; the prior 4.2% top is no longer reachable). FY2027 trimmed 7% -> 6% for the low Q4 exit rate; from FY2028 unchanged: the AI-native and Frontier AI Services pipeline (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft partnerships; AI-native >$185M in Q3 alone) and the new large deals convert, North America turns, and growth runs high-single digits before maturing. Still below the FY2016-2021 20%+ era.
bull.margin_rationale: Outcome-based AI engagements let EPAM keep a share of the productivity gain: pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 18% (terminal level unchanged), roughly the FY2019-21 level; the early years start from the higher FY2026 base.

bear.growth_rationale: Bottom of FY2026 guidance (3.5%), then UNCHANGED: the Software & Hi-Tech pattern (clients using AI tooling in-house, cutting external engineering hours) spreads to Financial Services and Consumer from FY2027; revenue declines ~4%/yr for two years and only stabilises at 1.5-2% nominal growth by FY2033. Q3 did not retire this path: three of six verticals shrank YoY and AI-native growth has not yet lifted the aggregate above low single digits. A Belarus/Ukraine escalation is not separately modelled but would sit inside this path.
bear.margin_rationale: Pricing deflation and bench cost during the contraction compress pre-SBC EBITDA from the 16.2% FY2026 level to 12% by FY2031 (trough level unchanged; the FY2023-24 trough was ~14%); SBC returns to a sticky ~3.9% because retention pay does not fall with revenue. Terminal cap 12x and growth 1.5% for a shrinking labour-arbitrage franchise. In this path the debt-funded ASR looks worst: ~$500M spent at roughly twice the bear value per share.

scenario_narratives.base: EPAM's axes are (1) whether generative-AI coding tools shrink billable hours faster than AI-native transformation work replaces them, (2) whether the large AI-led deals -- three now signed in Financial Services and Energy -- ramp through 2027 as promised, (3) Financial Services and Life Sciences growth versus Software & Hi-Tech decline, (4) whether the 2026 margin gain and the working-capital build that came with fixed-price work are durable, and (5) the Ukraine/Belarus delivery tail. Base: FY2026 lands at the raised 3.6% midpoint with pre-SBC EBITDA of 16.3%; FY2027 grows 3.5% off a soft Q4 exit, then 5% as the AI-native book converts partially, fading to 2.5% by FY2035 as AI productivity is largely passed to clients. Pre-SBC EBITDA edges to 17.0%; SBC eases from 3.7% to 3.0% of revenue; cash tax normalises from 31% to 25%. The $1.8B authorisation funds a flat ~48M share count. Net cash after the November ASR is ~$445M (less $25M restricted in Belarus), added once.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI turns out to be a demand multiplier for EPAM rather than a deflator: the frontier-model partnerships and Frontier AI Services make EPAM the engineering and integration layer for enterprise AI rollouts, the new large deals ramp on schedule, North America's two quarters of sequential growth become a recovery, and outcome-based pricing lets EPAM keep part of the productivity gain. Growth runs 6% in FY2027 and 8-9% in FY2028-30 before maturing to 3%; pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 18% (the FY2019-21 level). Terminal growth 3%, same 15x cap and 10.5% WACC as base. Here the November ASR was bought well below value.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Software & Hi-Tech vertical is the leading indicator: AI-savvy clients are already cutting external engineering hours and building in-house (the vertical fell ~6% YoY in Q3 2026), and from FY2027 Financial Services and Consumer clients follow as AI tooling matures. Time-and-materials revenue falls ~4%/yr for two years while EPAM carries bench cost and pricing deflation; pre-SBC EBITDA compresses to 12% and SBC stays sticky at ~3.9% of revenue. The business stabilises as a smaller, slower franchise (1.5% terminal growth, 12x cap). EPAM enters this path having swapped ~$500M of its cash cushion for shares at roughly twice their bear value, with a 50%-of-FCF return commitment through 2029 on top. This path is also where a Ukraine/Belarus escalation, large-deal slippage, or trapped-cash losses would land.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 30/45/25, deliberately. Q3 2026 cut both ways: for the bull, guidance was raised rather than slipped again, AI-native revenue reached ~13% of the quarter, and three large multiyear deals were signed; for the bear, aggregate growth is still 2.3% with Q4 guided flat, three of six verticals shrank YoY, operating cash flow fell by a third on working capital, and management has just levered a previously net-cash balance sheet to buy stock after a 20% jump. Bear stays at 30% (above the 15% default) because the thesis still rests on an unproven pivot from billable hours to outcome-based AI-native pricing and EPAM carries a geopolitical delivery tail no large peer shares. Bull stays at 25% (below the 35% default) because it still needs deal ramp, a North American recovery and favourable AI pricing together. FY2027 guidance at or above 4% organic growth with the working-capital build reversing would move bear toward 25%; a second guidance slip or a cut would move it toward 35%. The price move is not evidence and has not moved the weights.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC (incl. withholding taxes) fully expensed, interest income on the cash pile stripped, share count held flat, and a 10-year component build so the margin and tax paths have matured before Gordon growth is applied. The company is valued as a labour-based services franchise in structural transition, not as a software compounder: the terminal cap is 15x (12x bear), terminal growth 2.5%, and the AI-disruption risk is expressed through a 30% bear weight rather than a discount-rate premium so it is charged once. Since the September build the market has moved from pricing something between bear and base to pricing slightly above base; the model's value moved only a few dollars, because one quarter of better margins and a raised guide is a year-1 fact, not yet proof of the pivot. The debt-funded ASR is value-neutral in method (cash out, shares out) and slightly dilutive in fact, because it was struck above the weighted value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Generative-AI productivity reducing billable hours per project faster than AI-native revenue replaces them (structural, the bear axis)
The three new large deals and the wider AI-led pipeline failing to ramp through 2027; the Q4 2026 guide is flat YoY, so FY2027 growth depends on that ramp
Software & Hi-Tech decline spreading to Financial Services and Consumer as those clients build in-house

Working capital: 9M-2026 operating cash flow down a third on rising contract assets; if fixed-price and milestone billing permanently lengthen the cash cycle, the build's early-year owner FCF is ~$150M/yr too high

Leverage shift: ~$1.0B of 2026 buybacks against ~$450-500M of reported FCF, part-funded on the revolver, with a $1.8B authorisation and a 50%-of-FCF return floor through 2029; a move to sustained net debt in a bear path would warrant a higher discount rate
The pro forma share count (48.0M) and the cash/debt split of the ASR are estimates until the FY2026 10-K; each 0.5M shares is worth roughly 1% of value per share
Ukraine/Belarus escalation disrupting ~21% of delivery staff, the owned Kyiv building, and ~$53M of in-country cash
Cash tax rate staying near 35% rather than normalising to 25% (Section 174 timing, foreign withholding)
Interest income is estimated, not tagged; a higher true figure would lower the owner-FCF base modestly
Margin durability: the FY2026 margin gain came with cost discipline on barely growing revenue; roughly half of it is assumed to persist
